We really need a MRP to be able to troubleshoot this efficiently.

You could try to get a crash backtrace with debug symbols by [compiling the editor](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/contributing/development/compiling/compiling_for_macos.html) with `debug_symbols=yes`, but uploading a MRP is preferable.

I've done a git bisect of my project and found the earliest iteration that triggers the bug. It causes the same backtrace if I import into Godot 4.4, make sure Forward+ is selected, then exit the editor and run it from Godot's splash screen.
[ReptonGodotCrasher.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19632229/ReptonGodotCrasher.zip)

I downloaded godot from git today and built it with `scons platform=macos target=editor production=yes debug_symbols=yes`. I got the backtrace below, but I don't think it's much help. It looks like _canvas_texture_invalidation_callback is calling HashMap::erase with a bad reference to HashMap in this line:
```
		static_cast<RendererCanvasRenderRD *>(singleton)->canvas_texture_to_uniform_set.erase(kv->key);
```
That implies that singleton is a bad pointer, so I added a null check:
```
	if (p_deleted && singleton) {
		static_cast<RendererCanvasRenderRD *>(singleton)->canvas_texture_to_uniform_set.erase(kv->key);
	}
```
That seems to prevent the crash, but I don't know whether it's the correct solution or just masking a deeper issue.

Still reproducible in 4.6.3-stable on an M3 Pro (Metal 3.1, Forward+), so this made it into 4.6. Same fingerprint as above, a batch of leaked RIDs right before the crash:

```
WARNING: 4 RIDs of type "CanvasItem" were leaked.
WARNING: 17 RIDs of type "Texture" were leaked.
ERROR: 18 RID allocations of type 'N10RendererRD11MeshStorage4MeshE' were leaked at exit.
ERROR: 17 RID allocations of type 'N10RendererRD14TextureStorage7TextureE' were leaked at exit.
ERROR: 1 RID allocations of type 'N10RendererRD14TextureStorage13CanvasTextureE' were leaked at exit.
```

Two observations that might help narrow it down.

**It depends on what was loaded, not on how long the process ran.** Quitting from the initial menu scene is clean every time. Quitting after a gameplay level has been loaded and torn down crashes reproducibly (2/2 with a fixed recipe here). That lines up with the leaked RIDs: the crash seems to need orphaned render resources to exist in the first place.

**The faulting address is the same on every run: `0xaa0`, SEGV_ACCERR.** That is a field read through a null base, not a dangling pointer. I also ran the same scenarios with `MallocScribble=1` (macOS fills freed blocks with 0x55): the clean case stayed clean, and the faulting address never turned into `0x5555...`. So this doesn't look like a use-after-free on memory that happens to get reused, more like something being nulled or destroyed during teardown while the renderer still walks it.

The project is 2D only, which fits 6639174 being a 2D `CanvasTexture` change.

Caveat on my end: my build is a custom one (it embeds a JVM for scripting) and it is stripped, so native frames in my crash reports resolve to the nearest exported symbol and are misleading. I left them out for that reason rather than post a backtrace that points at the wrong functions. Happy to test a patch or gather more data on 4.6.3 if that helps.

@stan220 Could you test the modification from [my last comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104922#issuecomment-3679489465)? It fixes the crash for me, but I think it might just be a band aid that doesn't address the underlying issue.

@realh Tested your patch on my own project (2D game, Godot 4.6.3-stable, M3 Pro / macOS 14.7.4).

Setup: I built 4.6.3-stable from source (same commit as the binary I normally ship, 35e80b3a8). No Xcode on this machine, so I built with `metal=no vulkan=yes` and ran with `--rendering-driver vulkan` — the crash reproduces on MoltenVK exactly like on Metal, so it isn't Metal-specific.

The upside of a self-built (non-stripped) binary is that I finally got a readable backtrace, and it matches yours:

```
RendererCanvasRenderRD::_canvas_texture_invalidation_callback(bool, void*)
RendererRD::TextureStorage::~TextureStorage()
RendererCompositorRD::finalize()
RenderingServerDefault::_finish()
Main::cleanup(bool)
OS_MacOS_NSApp::cleanup()
__CFNOTIFICATIONCENTER_IS_CALLING_OUT_TO_AN_OBSERVER__
-[NSApplication run]
```

Same scenario every time (play through two levels, quit with Cmd+Q):

| build | result |
| --- | --- |
| stock 4.6.3 (Metal) | crash, signal 11 |
| my build, unpatched (Vulkan) | crash, backtrace above |
| my build with `if (p_deleted && singleton)` | 3/3 clean exits |

Worth noting: in the patched runs the exit state is identical to the crashing ones — same `59 RIDs of type "CanvasItem" were leaked` and the same `1 RID allocations of type CanvasTexture were leaked at exit`. So the destructor path still runs, the null check just keeps it from dereferencing a dead singleton.

I share your doubt that this is the real fix. `RendererCanvasRenderRD::singleton` is already null by the time `~TextureStorage` fires the invalidation callback, so the underlying problem seems to be the teardown order in `RendererCompositorRD::finalize()` — the canvas renderer is gone while texture storage still holds canvas textures whose destructors call back into it. The guard does make shutdown safe though, and I've seen no side effects so far.

One more data point that may help narrow it down: the crash only happens when there are leaked canvas resources at exit. Quitting from the main menu, or right after a level finishes, is always clean here; it needs orphaned canvas items/textures still alive when the app terminates.
